s1.syndrome_frame: Congenital cutaneous lesions with progressive growth and systemic involvement
salient_findings: Multiple cutaneous red papules since birth
Lesions with ulceration and bleeding
Numerous bright red macules, papules, and plaques on the head, neck, trunk, extremities, and other areas
Hemorrhagic crust and dark scale on some lesions
Retrognathia, thickened maxillary frenulum, and anterior ankyloglossia
key_facts: Patient is a 3-month-old boy
Born at full term via spontaneous vaginal delivery
No prenatal care
No history of environmental or hazardous substance exposure
Paternal family history is unremarkable
Maternal family history is unknown
Physical examination revealed numerous cutaneous lesions
Laboratory tests, including complete blood cell count and metabolic panel, are normal
Abdominal ultrasonography is normal
Brain MRI showed enhancing nodule, exophytic soft tissue polyps, and mild hypogenesis/dysgenesis of corpus callosum
Histopathology showed upper dermal lobulated capillary proliferation
Immunohistochemistry results are positive for CD31 and smooth muscle actin (SMA), and negative for D2-40 and GLUT-1
Genetic testing is negative for several genes, including ATR, BRAF, FLT4, GNA14, HRAS, KDR, KRAS, and NRAS

shortlist.label: Kasabach-Merritt Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: ulceration and bleeding of cutaneous lesions, presence of enhancing nodule and exophytic soft tissue polyps on brain MRI

shortlist.label: Kaposiform Hemangioendothelioma
shortlist.why_kept: histopathology showing upper dermal lobulated capillary proliferation, positive immunohistochemistry for CD31 and SMA

shortlist.label: Tufted Angioma
shortlist.why_kept: presence of multiple cutaneous lesions with hemorrhagic crust and dark scale, positive immunohistochemistry for CD31 and SMA

shortlist.label: Congenital Hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: presence of cutaneous lesions at birth, progressive growth of lesions, and presence of enhancing nodule on brain MRI

shortlist.label: Infantile Hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: presence of multiple cutaneous lesions, positive immunohistochemistry for CD31, and typical age of presentation

raw.rationale: The presence of multiple cutaneous red papules with ulceration and bleeding, along with the histopathology showing upper dermal lobulated capillary proliferation and immunohistochemistry results positive for CD31 and smooth muscle actin (SMA), supports the diagnosis of Kaposiform Hemangioendothelioma. The condition is also associated with the Kasabach-Merritt phenomenon, but the key distinguishing feature here is the specific histopathological and immunohistochemical findings.

rejected.label: Kasabach-Merritt Syndrome
rejected.why: While Kasabach-Merritt Syndrome is a consideration due to the presence of bleeding and thrombocytopenia is not mentioned, the specific histopathological findings point more towards Kaposiform Hemangioendothelioma.

rejected.label: Tufted Angioma
rejected.why: Tufted angioma is a possibility but the description of the lesions and the histopathological findings, particularly the positivity for CD31 and SMA, are more characteristic of Kaposiform Hemangioendothelioma.

rejected.label: Congenital Hemangioma
rejected.why: Congenital hemangiomas are typically fully formed at birth and involute by 1-2 years of age, the description provided does not fully align with this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Infantile Hemangioma
rejected.why: Infantile hemangiomas usually appear after birth, grow rapidly during the first year, and then involute. The presence of lesions at birth and the specific histological features do not align well with infantile hemangioma.
